correctness.rationale: A volume-uniform point admits exactly the linear-extension rank representation. Dirichlet order-statistic moments determine each rational covariance entry, and the block-permutation representation diagonalizes the matrix. The two exact determinants det(B-alpha_p I) and det(B-alpha_q I) establish which eigenvalue is least, including all integer boundaries. The all-ones Rayleigh quotient is 1/12 for every pair and the positive near-balanced trace/determinant identity gives the strict fourfold threshold. The proof covers all integer p,q with 2<=p<=q. The standalone exact-rational checker independently exhausts 17 small rank-assignment profiles (869 entries), plus 6084 spectral parameter profiles; finite tests alone do not prove infinite statements.

originality.rationale: Inspected primary full-text face-vector papers and two prior public complete-height-two John ellipsoid results use the same objects but do not state the normalized-volume inertia covariance or its sharp fourfold transition. The classification of covariance eigenmodes is neither an f-vector statement nor a consequence of the John matrix (an extremal inscribed-ellipsoid shape). No equivalent or broader statement was found in the actual compared sources; generic known simplex moment formulas are methodological inputs, not the evaluated infinite-family spectral inequalities. Worldwide historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: An unexamined general formula for all order-polytope moments might imply these entries and comparison after specialization; historical priority is not certified.

value.rationale: The standard-Euclidean covariance of a uniform point is a natural geometric inertia invariant for order polytopes and, unlike known volume and face numbers, measures anisotropy. The result completely classifies the spectrum and multiplicities for an infinite two-parameter maximal-ranked-poset family, locates a sharp change of least-variance eigenspace after the second extra antichain element, and proves a nonattained universal fourfold condition-number boundary. The balanced formula and one-sided asymptotic distinguish nontrivial geometric regimes; no downstream conjecture or unverified application is claimed.
